title: Uniqueness of cartesian symmetric monoidal structures over a fixed underlying equivalence
statement:
Use the infinity-category, mapping-space and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and symmetric monoidal infinity categories and strong functors of [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification]. Let $p:\mathcal A^\otimes\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and $q:\mathcal B^\otimes\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be symmetric monoidal infinity categories, with underlying infinity categories $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$. Assume both structures are cartesian: their units $\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}$ and $\mathbf1_{\mathcal B}$ are terminal, and the canonical maps $a\otimes a'\to a\otimes\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}\simeq a$ and $a\otimes a'\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}\otimes a'\simeq a'$ exhibit the tensor as the product for all $a,a'\in\mathcal A$, and likewise in $\mathcal B$. The canonical maps here are induced by the terminal maps to the unit and the unit equivalences. Write $\operatorname{Eq}^{\otimes}(\mathcal A^\otimes,\mathcal B^\otimes)$ for the space of equivalences over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ preserving all cocartesian edges, with their invertible natural transformations and higher homotopies; write $\operatorname{Eq}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ for the space of equivalences of the underlying infinity categories. Then restriction to the fiber over $\langle1\rangle$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Eq}^{\otimes}(\mathcal A^\otimes,\mathcal B^\otimes)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Eq}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B).$$
Equivalently, for every specified equivalence $u:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal B$, the space of strong symmetric monoidal equivalences $U:\mathcal A^\otimes\simeq\mathcal B^\otimes$ together with a specified natural equivalence $U|_{\mathcal A}\simeq u$ is contractible. These spaces are homotopy fibers, so the comparison with $u$ and all its homotopies are retained.
